en.toc_s7: The Object Pipeline vs Text Streams
en.s7_title: The Object Pipeline vs Text Streams
en.s1_intro: Unlike traditional text-based shells (such as Bash or CMD), PowerShell is an **object-oriented automation engine** built directly on top of the **.NET Common Language Runtime (CLR)**. Commands are structured natively as **Cmdlets** adhering to a standard, predictable Verb-Noun syntax design.
en.s2_intro: By default, Windows blocks script executions to defend against malicious injections. PowerShell uses **Execution Policies** to determine whether untrusted configuration scripts can be processed inside your runtime thread.
en.s3_intro: PowerShell uses abstraction layers called **Providers** to expose various data repositories—such as the Windows Registry, environment variables, or local certificate silos—as if they were standard file system drives.
en.s4_intro: Variables are prefixed with the dollar symbol ($). Because they wrap full **.NET Objects**, you can dynamically query properties or pass variable payloads explicitly to typed constraint fields.
en.s5_intro: PowerShell does not use standard symbols (like > or ==) for comparison logic, because those tokens are reserved for stream redirection. Instead, it relies on dedicated **dash-based operators**.
en.s6_intro: PowerShell provides classic control loops along with the highly optimized ForEach-Object pipeline cmdlet, which evaluates incoming elements sequentially via the automatic pipeline variable $_.
en.s7_intro: When you pipe data in PowerShell, you are passing full, structured objects rather than raw strings of text. This design avoids complex regex filtering or text splitting (like awk or cut), allowing you to filter, sort, or inspect fields directly by their property names.
en.s8_intro: PowerShell interfaces directly with the host operating system kernel using the **CIM (Common Information Model)** architecture, enabling comprehensive instrumentation and management of both local and remote nodes.

it.s8_title: Amministrazione Remota con WinRM e PowerShell Remoting
it.s1_intro: I comandi PowerShell seguono una convenzione coerente di Verbo-Sostantivo (come Get-Process o Set-Service) per la massima intuitività.
it.s2_intro: A differenza delle shell Unix che trasmettono testo grezzo, la pipeline di PowerShell trasporta veri e propri oggetti .NET dotati di proprietà e metodi.
it.s3_intro: I comandi di filtro estraggono proprietà mirate ed escludono record non rilevanti direttamente durante il transito nella pipeline.
it.s4_intro: Le variabili utilizzano il prefisso $ e integrano tutti i tipi di dato della piattaforma .NET, con conversioni automatiche intelligenti.
it.s5_intro: Aggiungendo [CmdletBinding()] le funzioni create dallo sviluppatore acquisiscono parametri comuni come -Verbose e -ErrorAction.
it.s6_intro: PowerShell distingue tra errori bloccanti e non bloccanti, consentendo di intercettarli accuratamente con blocchi try/catch/finally.
it.s7_intro: I provider permettono di navigare registri di sistema, certificati e variabili di ambiente con gli stessi comandi usati per il disco (es. dir o cd).
it.s8_intro: Il comando Invoke-Command esegue blocchi di script su centinaia di server contemporaneamente attraverso connessioni sicure crittografate.

es.s7_title: Proveedores PSDrive y el Registro de Windows
es.s1_intro: Las utilidades de PowerShell siguen un estándar intuitivo compuesto por un verbo de acción y un sustantivo objetivo, como Get-Service.
es.s2_intro: A diferencia de consolas tradicionales de texto, la tubería de PowerShell transporta instancias vivas de objetos .NET con métodos interactivos.
es.s3_intro: Los comandos Where-Object y Select-Object extraen campos específicos y descartan elementos según condiciones lógicas.
es.s4_intro: Las variables anteponen el prefijo $ y pueden forzar tipos de datos específicos mediante la sintaxis de tipos de .NET.
es.s5_intro: Habilitar [CmdletBinding()] en una función personalizada proporciona soporte nativo para parámetros del sistema como -Verbose y confirmaciones.
es.s6_intro: Combinar -ErrorAction Stop con bloques try/catch asegura la captura de fallos de comando para evitar interrupciones no deseadas.
es.s7_intro: Los PSDrives permiten inspeccionar almacenes de certificados, variables de entorno y el registro de Windows usando comandos de navegación de carpetas.
es.s8_intro: La administración distribuida permite despachar comandos en paralelo sobre múltiples máquinas remotas de forma segura mediante WinRM o SSH.
